llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements are consistent with a wallet-based Nigerian airtime/data purchase tool, but it persists auth tokens locally and calls an external API of unknown provenance — exercise caution before giving it real money or letting it run autonomously.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included files and SKILL.md. The three Node.js helpers generate order/device IDs and manage a session token, which are appropriate for a payment/checkout integration; no unrelated env vars, binaries, or config paths are requested.

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrowly scoped to the payment flow and use only the documented API endpoints. They instruct running the included Node scripts and persisting .session_token and .device_id in the skill directory. Be aware the 'load' command prints the session token to stdout, which could leak if the agent transmits outputs.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims (buy airtime/data) and includes small helper scripts to manage device IDs and session tokens. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify and trust the external API domain (https://lodu.bleon.net) and the skill's author — there is no homepage or publisher information in the registry metadata. 2) Test with a throwaway or low-value wallet first — do not connect a production/funded account until you confirm behavior. 3) Note that .session_token and .device_id are written into the skill directory; treat these files as sensitive (anyone or any process with access could use them to make orders). 4) Be cautious about allowing the agent to invoke this skill autonomously (it can place orders); consider requiring explicit user confirmation for any purchase. 5) You can review the three included JS files locally (they are small and readable) to satisfy yourself they match the documented behavior.
